headline.name: pq2_readme.direction_evidence_for_bounded_degree_premise
headline.note: Encoded judgment, recomputed from repository data: a constant step degree on n = 17..34 is evidence for a bounded degree only if nothing in the repository shows this family's degree rising. Two records do: (1) the msolve data themselves take the values [3, 4] on n = 8..34 (3 at n <= 14 and n = 16, 4 at n = 15 and from n = 17); (2) the corpus's own record MEAS-GB-KW-TABLE1 (docs/ecdlp-hardness-corpus/lit-groebner.json) gives, for the same family (m = 2, n = 34..48), Magma highest step degree 4 for n <= 36 and 5 for n = 37..48, i.e. the next step lies just past the msolve window (n <= 34). A two-fold window in n cannot discriminate a bounded degree from a slowly growing one (cf. the LOG fit in research/fall_degree_bounds_20261008/RESULTS.md). Supported wording: 'the degree is 4 on every instance from n = 17 to 34, matching Kousidis-Wiemers' value 4 for n <= 36; they report 5 from n = 37, so these data neither support nor refute a bounded degree'.
